title: Broad Lean Corpus Build and Rich Isomorphism Status v0

canonical_node.axiom: The broader Lean corpus contains a richer structural testing layer that goes beyond equation-shape analogy, and this layer is verified by a successful full build with no active proof escapes.
definitions: Rich isomorphism: a mapping that preserves roles, transitions, signature discipline, gate behavior, and passes adversarial wrong-swap checks.
Proof escape: active use of sorry, admit, axiom, or unsafe in source files (excluding expected #check_failure diagnostics).
Seed kernel: a clean compressed assumption spine with 4 front-loaded assumptions and 17 no-sorry starter theorems.
Broad corpus: a richer formal archive with full build passed and reported 287 theorems / zero sorry / zero admit.
derivation: The full build command 'lake build' completed successfully with 17 jobs.
The proof-escape scan found no active sorry, admit, axiom, or unsafe in main source files.
The build output includes 'have this := sorry' from #check_failure diagnostics, which are expected and not active proof holes.
Targeted builds for Theophysics_Core, Theophysics_Adversarial, and other modules passed.
The corpus contains RichLawIso, richLaw4Iso, no_rich_iso_to_natural_coin, richRelabeledCoinIso, BridgeMatrix, MasterEquationInvariance, and wrong-swap rejection rows.
The upgraded layer tests role preservation, transition preservation, signature discipline, gate behavior, and adversarial wrong-swap failures.
The intended mappings pass inside the encoded model while selected false mappings fail.
canonical_node.action: Maintain the broad corpus as a separate build layer from the seed kernel. Continue to verify the rich isomorphism layer through full builds and proof-escape scans. Do not merge the broad corpus into the seed package until the theorem inventory is normalized and wrapper/trivial rows are separated from substantive theorem rows.
boundary: Lean verifies the encoded structure, not the domain-faithfulness of human labels.
Physics, theology, history, and source-grounding still carry the burden of domain fidelity.
The reported 287 theorems are corpus claims, not independently verified by this document.
The build success does not prove that every human label is domain-faithful.
test: Run 'lake build' and confirm successful completion.
Run the proof-escape scan and confirm no active sorry, admit, axiom, or unsafe in main source files.
Verify that the rich isomorphism layer includes the listed components (RichLawIso, richLaw4Iso, etc.).

overstatement_risks: Claiming that Lean proves domain-faithfulness of human labels.
Treating the reported 287 theorems as independently verified without normalization.
Assuming the rich isomorphism layer is fully sound without inspecting the actual Lean code.
kill_conditions: If a full build fails on the current toolchain.
If active sorry/admit/axiom/unsafe are found in main source files.
If the rich isomorphism layer is shown to be vacuous or not actually testing the claimed properties.
risk.lean_target: Formalize the rich isomorphism layer in Lean, ensuring that the intended mappings pass and false mappings fail, with no proof escapes.

plain_summary: This document reports that a broad Lean corpus builds successfully and contains a richer isomorphism testing layer beyond simple equation-shape analogy. It includes signature discipline, role/transition preservation, gate tests, and adversarial wrong-swap checks. The build passed and no active proof escapes were found, but the document cautions against overclaiming domain-faithfulness and recommends keeping the broad corpus separate from the seed kernel until the theorem inventory is normalized.
